trial.title: Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS) Dose-Escalation Study for Brain Metastasis

endpoints.description: To identify the maximal tolerated doses for single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery, within 90 days from the date of procedure, in patients with brain metastases who have not undergone prior brain irradiation.
To evaluate the overall survival (OS), which is defined as the time between date of SRS and the date of death due to any cause.

To evaluate time to progression (TTP), which is defined as the time between date of SRS and date of documented progression. Specific TTP will be determined for the target lesion, non-target lesions, and elsewhere in brain.

To evaluate the local progression rate of the target lesion. Local progression will be defined by MRI (with or without contrast)/CT (with contrast) imaging according to the modified RECIST 1.1 criteria. Suspected radiation necrosis and/or pseudoprogression will be similarly evaluated
To evaluate the response rate, consisting of complete response (CR) and partial response according to the modified RECIST 1.1.

analysis_trace.finding: NCT02645487 is a Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for brain metastases without whole brain radiation. Single-group design with 135 estimated enrollment. Primary objective: identify maximal tolerated doses (MTD) within 90 days. Secondary: OS, TTP, local progression rate, response rate over 3 years. Dose levels: ≤1cm: 24→30Gy; >1-2cm: 21→27Gy; >2-3cm: 18→24Gy.

Adults with biopsy-proven non-hematopoietic malignancy (excluding SCLC, germ cell, unknown primary), 1-10 brain metastases, all <3cm, outside brainstem, no prior brain radiation, ECOG ≤2. Mixed primary tumor types expected (NSCLC, breast, melanoma, renal cell carcinoma).

SRS delivers high-dose ablative radiation to discrete brain lesions. Dose escalation aims to improve local control while identifying dose-limiting toxicity (radiation necrosis, symptomatic edema, neurological decline).

primary-0: MTD defined by dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) within 90 days using 3+3 or similar escalation. Success=MTD identified for at least one size stratum. secondary-0: OS is standard survival endpoint. secondary-1: TTP requires radiographic assessment. secondary-2: Local progression rate uses modified RECIST 1.1. secondary-3: Response rate (CR+PR) by modified RECIST 1.1.

Expected DLTs: symptomatic radiation necrosis requiring steroids or surgery, grade ≥3 neurological toxicity, severe edema. Historical SRS at 24Gy for ≤1cm lesions shows ~5-10% symptomatic necrosis; escalation to 30Gy may increase toxicity. Larger lesions have higher necrosis risk at equivalent doses.

1) Dose escalation may reach toxicity before efficacy plateau, limiting therapeutic window. 2) Single-arm design without comparative control for secondary endpoints. 3) Heterogeneous primary histologies confound response/outcome predictions. 4) 3-year follow-up may be incomplete at analysis. 5) Radiation necrosis vs tumor progression discrimination challenges.

Evidence: (1) Protocol snapshot confirms design but no results (use=trial design only). (2) Literature search returned related studies but fetch failed for all URLs; no direct numeric evidence usable. (3) Background knowledge: Phase I dose-escalation studies historically succeed in identifying MTD (~80-90% completion). SRS for brain mets established: 24Gy standard for ≤1cm, 18-21Gy for 2-3cm. Escalation to 30Gy/27Gy/24Gy likely tolerable for smaller lesions but toxicity increases with size. OS for brain mets historically 6-12 months median without systemic therapy advances. Local control at 12 months ~70-90% with standard SRS. Response rates variable by histology.

No retrieved outcome data for this specific trial. No direct numeric evidence from literature search (fetch failures). Reliance on general SRS literature and Phase I trial completion patterns. Expected completion March 2025 per registry; results not yet available at cutoff.

analysis_trace.finding: NCT02645487 is a Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for brain metastases without whole brain radiation. Single-group design with 135 estimated enrollment. Primary objective: identify maximal tolerated doses (MTD) within 90 days. Secondary: OS, TTP, local progression rate, response rate over 3 years. Dose levels: ≤1cm: 24→30Gy; >1-2cm: 21→27Gy; >2-3cm: 18→24Gy.

Adults with biopsy-proven non-hematopoietic malignancy (excluding SCLC, germ cell, unknown primary), 1-10 brain metastases, all <3cm, outside brainstem, no prior brain radiation, ECOG ≤2. Mixed primary tumor types expected (NSCLC, breast, melanoma, renal cell carcinoma).

SRS delivers high-dose ablative radiation to discrete brain lesions. Dose escalation aims to improve local control while identifying dose-limiting toxicity (radiation necrosis, symptomatic edema, neurological decline).

primary-0: MTD defined by dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) within 90 days using 3+3 or similar escalation. Success=MTD identified for at least one size stratum. secondary-0: OS is standard survival endpoint. secondary-1: TTP requires radiographic assessment. secondary-2: Local progression rate uses modified RECIST 1.1. secondary-3: Response rate (CR+PR) by modified RECIST 1.1.

Expected DLTs: symptomatic radiation necrosis requiring steroids or surgery, grade ≥3 neurological toxicity, severe edema. Historical SRS at 24Gy for ≤1cm lesions shows ~5-10% symptomatic necrosis; escalation to 30Gy may increase toxicity. Larger lesions have higher necrosis risk at equivalent doses.

1) Dose escalation may reach toxicity before efficacy plateau, limiting therapeutic window. 2) Single-arm design without comparative control for secondary endpoints. 3) Heterogeneous primary histologies confound response/outcome predictions. 4) 3-year follow-up may be incomplete at analysis. 5) Radiation necrosis vs tumor progression discrimination challenges.

Evidence: (1) Protocol snapshot confirms design but no results (use=trial design only). (2) Literature search returned related studies but fetch failed for all URLs; no direct numeric evidence usable. (3) Background knowledge: Phase I dose-escalation studies historically succeed in identifying MTD (~80-90% completion). SRS for brain mets established: 24Gy standard for ≤1cm, 18-21Gy for 2-3cm. Escalation to 30Gy/27Gy/24Gy likely tolerable for smaller lesions but toxicity increases with size. OS for brain mets historically 6-12 months median without systemic therapy advances. Local control at 12 months ~70-90% with standard SRS. Response rates variable by histology.

No retrieved outcome data for this specific trial. No direct numeric evidence from literature search (fetch failures). Reliance on general SRS literature and Phase I trial completion patterns. Expected completion March 2025 per registry; results not yet available at cutoff.

你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。
14. 如果提到模型既有知识中的外部试验或论文，但当前会话没有成功检索并冻结其内容，必须明确标注为“未核验背景先验/假设”，不得写入 search_verification，也不得伪装成已查到的引用。
15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。
16. 每条外部资料在使用前必须核对人群、药物/剂量、适应证、endpoint定义、测量单位、时间点、对照组和estimand。完全匹配的资料才可支持精确数值；同药物或相近人群资料通常只能支持方向或范围。
17. 不同药物、不同适应证、明显不同人群或不同endpoint的资料只能作为机制/背景资料，不能复制其精确效应量、置信区间或成功概率。明显不匹配的资料必须标记为 rejected_mismatch，并排除出核心证据链。
18. 对每条重要资料说明 evidence_role：direct_numeric、indirect_direction、mechanism_background 或 rejected_mismatch，并说明 mismatch_reason 和 numeric_use_allowed。没有匹配数字锚点时仍须预测已定义终点，但要扩大不确定性、降低confidence并说明外推距离；不能仅因证据间接而使用 not_evaluable。
19. 如果动态装载的试验上下文已经包含设计、组别、endpoint、时间点、人群和统计字段，不需要搜索NCT；只有字段缺失或有歧义时才允许最多一次registry_record用于设计核实。不得搜索NCT结果替代结局证据，也不得使用截止日后的注册结果。

最终只输出一个严格 JSON 对象。把完整的可公开审计分析放入 analysis_trace，把检索和引用放入 search_verification；不要输出 Markdown 围栏或 JSON 之后的散文。

analysis_trace.finding: NCT02645487 is a Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for brain metastases without whole brain radiation. Single-group design with 135 estimated enrollment. Primary objective: identify maximal tolerated doses (MTD) within 90 days. Secondary: OS, TTP, local progression rate, response rate over 3 years. Dose levels: ≤1cm: 24→30Gy; >1-2cm: 21→27Gy; >2-3cm: 18→24Gy.

Adults with biopsy-proven non-hematopoietic malignancy (excluding SCLC, germ cell, unknown primary), 1-10 brain metastases, all <3cm, outside brainstem, no prior brain radiation, ECOG ≤2. Mixed primary tumor types expected (NSCLC, breast, melanoma, renal cell carcinoma).

SRS delivers high-dose ablative radiation to discrete brain lesions. Dose escalation aims to improve local control while identifying dose-limiting toxicity (radiation necrosis, symptomatic edema, neurological decline).

primary-0: MTD defined by dose-limiting toxicities (DLT) within 90 days using 3+3 or similar escalation. Success=MTD identified for at least one size stratum. secondary-0: OS is standard survival endpoint. secondary-1: TTP requires radiographic assessment. secondary-2: Local progression rate uses modified RECIST 1.1. secondary-3: Response rate (CR+PR) by modified RECIST 1.1.

Expected DLTs: symptomatic radiation necrosis requiring steroids or surgery, grade ≥3 neurological toxicity, severe edema. Historical SRS at 24Gy for ≤1cm lesions shows ~5-10% symptomatic necrosis; escalation to 30Gy may increase toxicity. Larger lesions have higher necrosis risk at equivalent doses.

1) Dose escalation may reach toxicity before efficacy plateau, limiting therapeutic window. 2) Single-arm design without comparative control for secondary endpoints. 3) Heterogeneous primary histologies confound response/outcome predictions. 4) 3-year follow-up may be incomplete at analysis. 5) Radiation necrosis vs tumor progression discrimination challenges.

Evidence: (1) Protocol snapshot confirms design but no results (use=trial design only). (2) Literature search returned related studies but fetch failed for all URLs; no direct numeric evidence usable. (3) Background knowledge: Phase I dose-escalation studies historically succeed in identifying MTD (~80-90% completion). SRS for brain mets established: 24Gy standard for ≤1cm, 18-21Gy for 2-3cm. Escalation to 30Gy/27Gy/24Gy likely tolerable for smaller lesions but toxicity increases with size. OS for brain mets historically 6-12 months median without systemic therapy advances. Local control at 12 months ~70-90% with standard SRS. Response rates variable by histology.

No retrieved outcome data for this specific trial. No direct numeric evidence from literature search (fetch failures). Reliance on general SRS literature and Phase I trial completion patterns. Expected completion March 2025 per registry; results not yet available at cutoff.
